messages:
Matt: quick check — noticed on-prem (dc1 baremetal) 95/99th token latency is ~2-3x higher than hosted for the same model + input. suspect CPU freq scaling/turbo behavior. anyone seen this before?

Ayana: can you paste a small snapshot of sys info + perf numbers? even cpupower / scaling_governor output helps.

Matt: pasted from dc1-bm-07:```hostname: dc1-bm-07
cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor: powersave
cpupower frequency-info: driver: intel_pstate
  CPUs which run at the same hardware frequency: 0-23
  hardware limits: 800 MHz - 3.8 GHz
  available cpufreq governors: performance, powersave

perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -r 5 ./inference_bench --seed 42
  avg cycles: 2.1e9  instructions: 1.3e9  cache-misses: 4.2e6
  p95 latency: 160ms  p99: 270ms
```

Jin: thanks. two quick things: (1) "powersave" causes cpufreq to stay low unless load is sustained — for short bursts (small requests) you hit lower P-states and pay a ramp penalty. (2) check turbo boost and intel_pstate mode. run `turbostat -i 2 -S` while doing the bench to see C-state/Turbo.

Suresh: agreed. on host pools where we pin to performance governor we see ~30-40% tail reduction for small token batches. also check irq affinity + isolcpus — we had migration noise on these boxes.

Ayana: can we try a quick experiment? Matt, if you can on dc1-bm-07: `sudo cpupower frequency-set -g performance` then re-run the bench 3x and paste p95/p99. also `sudo modprobe msr; sudo turbostat -n 5 1` during run.

Matt: running now, will post results in ~10m.

ops-bot: FYI — scheduled a maintenance window for dc1-bm-07 at +1h if sysadmin changes are needed. (admins: @Suresh @Jin) :calendar: 

Matt: quick follow-up numbers after switching governor:```before (powersave) p95: 160ms p99: 270ms
after (performance)  p95: 110ms p99: 150ms
perf shows cycles down ~22% and much fewer frequency ramps in turbostat output.```

Jin: nice. that matches microbench expectations. can you also try toggling intel_pstate=disable in kernel cmdline (reboot) to see if acpi cpufreq behaves differently? no need to do now if ops blocks reboot.

Suresh: also let's check NIC rx/tx interrupt coalescing and RPS. small requests can be affected by NIC latency too. Matt, can you paste `ethtool -c eth0` and `cat /proc/interrupts | grep eth0`?

Matt: pasted ethtool and /proc/interrupts in a gist (link removed here for thread brevity). IRQs mostly on cpu0, no RPS configured.

Ayana: plan: (1) make a perf playbook for dc1: set governor to performance on inference nodes, tune IRQ affinity + enable RPS, capture turbostat/perf snapshots; (2) run A/B for 24h on a small canary pool; (3) if stable, add as an ops-runbook (and document regression risk).

Matt: sounds good. I'll create the canary with 10 nodes and tag them `onprem-cpufreq-canary` and run the load harness. pinging @Jin @Suresh for assist on RPS/irq steps.

Jin: happy to help. I can provide a small script to set irq affinity + enable RPS via sysfs. will drop it in the ops-runbook repo.

Suresh: +1. once we have stable numbers we should add a telemetry check to Console (token-level tail diff vs hosted) so regressions get alerted.

Matt: thanks all — will post the run summary and raw logs when done. :thumbsup:
